messages:
Alex G: Quick q — we need a safe pattern to grant temporary per-API-key burst capacity to internal partners (connectors, telemetry ingest, partner infra). Current key-level overrides are too coarse and create audit + billing headaches. Sketch below — looking for production concerns and missing pieces.

Maria T: SG. what's the threat model? who can request these grants? :thinking_face:

Alex G: Initial idea: only service accounts owned by product/infra teams can request. Flow: 1) create a 'temporary override' in Console, pick key(s), set add_qps + burst_tokens, expiry, justification, optional approver. 2) Console mints short-lived signed override token and writes override entry to WAL + in-memory map. 3) Rate-limiter applies override_id on evaluation, and telemetry tags metrics. 4) Auto-revoke at expiry + audit entry.

Devon K: We need a cryptographic guarantee the override came from Console (not curl). Mint a signed override token (JWT-like) that the rate-limiter validates. Include override_id, exp, signer_kid.

Samir P: Agree. Also decide semantics vs existing org quotas: are overrides additive or replace base limits? I think additive but bounded by a hard cap to prevent runaway. e.g., effective_qps = base_qps + min(override_add, hard_cap - base_qps).

Jin L: Console UX notes: modal "Grant temporary burst" with: target key(s), duration, added QPS, burst tokens, cost estimate, affected routes, approver dropdown, required justification. Show previous overrides for that key and a quick audit link.

Rebecca S: Telemetry: tag all request metrics with override_id, override_type, granted_qps, expires_at. Emit override.accounting{override_id,consumed_tokens} so billing can reconcile. Alert when override consumption >80% of granted or when cost delta > threshold.

ops-bot: rate-limiter-config: change applied to rl-cluster-prod-1 at 2026-03-18T10:20Z (dry-run) :white_check_mark:

Alex G: Quick config sketch we can hand to runtime team:

```json
{
  "override_id": "ovr-20260318-az9",
  "keys": ["svc-ingest-key"],
  "add_qps": 100,
  "burst_tokens": 2000,
  "expires_at": "2026-03-18T11:20:00Z",
  "requester": "service-account:infra-ingest",
  "signed_token": "eyJhbGciOi..."
}
```

Maria T: For security: require approver for grants over X QPS (configurable). Also maintain a deny-list of keys that are ineligible (system/backbone keys). Approver must be an SRE or product owner.

Devon K: Runtime notes: rate-limiter must consult an in-memory active-overrides map (watch WAL/kvstore). Do not do a DB call per request. Keep evaluation O(1). Sync via pubsub; TTL sync window must be <1s for strictness but can be eventual for lower-risk grants.

Samir P: For audit/compliance, writes must go to immutable WAL and S3 snapshots (retention 7y). Also emit events to the event stream for downstream billing pipelines.

Jin L: Rollout plan: behind feature flag per-org -> internal-only alpha with infra teams -> opt-in partners -> broad rollout. Console should expose the feature flag and audit log to admins.

Rebecca S: Add UI for revoke + reason + TTL extension (with re-approval workflow). Also show projected cost impact when requesting.

Alex G: Edge cases: what if a key is rotated while an override is active? We should bind overrides to key-id and also to owning-service id; rotations produce a new key-id so old overrides should either migrate or be invalidated. Thoughts?

Devon K: Invalidate by default on rotate unless the rotation flow explicitly migrates overrides (recommended for low-risk infra keys).

Maria T: Also require minimum approver count for very large grants (2 approvers for >1000 qps). Log approver ids in the override record.

Samir P: Emit metrics override.grants{team,approved_by,override_id} and override.revokes{reason,override_id}. Throttle the number of active overrides per-team to avoid abuse.

Alex G: Good call on throttles. We'll also limit total added_qps across active overrides per-key.

Jin L: UX smalls: when creating override show a one-line checklist for compliance: approver, justification, cost estimate, affected routes. Make the modal pre-populate approver based on team ownership.

Rebecca S: Add a periodic audit job that looks for overrides with low usage — auto-suggest revoke to owners.

Alex G: I'll draft a spec + mockups and a runtime PR. Tagging @Maria T and @Devon K for security and runtime review. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:

Maria T: Quick nit — include a 'sensitivity' classification on overrides (low/medium/high) that drives approver count and retention policy.

Devon K: Also add a deny-list for overrides at cluster level (some clusters for compliance can't accept temp grants).

Samir P: Final ask: ensure telemetry includes a flag override_source (console|api|automation) so we can filter automated grants.

Alex G: Great. I'll push a draft later today and post for review. End of thread.
